Published online:
    September 1, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Global (US, Japan, UK, France, Euro Zone, Asia, Iran)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — recaps Tuesday's market moves
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — Sept 15-16 FOMC meeting, upcoming CPI/PPI data, near-term rate hike probability
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — G7 fiscal sustainability, structural debt servicing concerns, persistent inflation regime

Synopsis:
    A global bond selloff is accelerating, driven by sticky inflation, rising oil prices (tied to an ongoing US-Israeli war on Iran), and deepening concern over G7 fiscal trajectories. Japan yields are breaking 30-year highs. Fed Governor Barr, viewed as a centrist, signaled he would vote for a rate hike at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting if CPI data doesn't soften — a meaningful hawkish shift. Fed Funds futures price a 66% hike / 34% hold. Manufacturing data globally was broadly resilient, led by AI hardware demand in Asia and a Euro zone beat, though US factory growth cooled on inflation/pricing concerns.

---

Relevance: YES — while the article is global in scope, the US rate outlook (Fed Governor Barr's hawkish signal, FOMC September meeting, Fed Funds futures pricing) is the central actionable narrative for markets.

Sentiment: 75 (More hawkish than before) — A centrist FOMC member explicitly flagging a September hike vote, three prior July dissents, and Fed Funds futures tilting 2:1 toward a hike collectively mark a clear hawkish shift from prior positioning. The tone is decisive and urgency-driven, not exploratory.
